content: Bedaquiline, marketed under the brand name SIRTURO, is formulated for oral administration and is available in 100 mg strength tablets. Each tablet contains 89 mg of bedaquiline fumarate, which is chemically equivalent to 100 mg of bedaquiline. Bedaquiline is classified as a diarylquinoline antimycobacterial agent. The fumarate salt of bedaquiline appears as a white to nearly white powder and is practically insoluble in aqueous media. The chemical name of bedaquiline fumarate is (1R, 2S)-1-(6-bromo-2-methoxy-3-quinolinyl)-4-(dimethylamino)-2-(1-naphthalenyl)-1-phenyl-2-butanol compound with fumaric acid (1:1). The inactive ingredients in the formulation include lactose monohydrate, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, polysorbate 20, and purified water (which is removed during processing).
